findings.reason: The documented contract sets a maximum, and the supplied normal dispatch path checks equality before each insertion. It removes the waiting request before dispatch, and doQueueRequest adds it to queuedRequests_ before any recursive completion can dispatch another request. Completion removes queued entries before re-entering dispatch. Stop separately moves waiting requests out, then directly adds cancelled requests for ordered completion after stopDevice; those requests do not reach queueRequestDevice. The supplied paths support the claim without assuming an over-limit prestate or proving an invariant across the whole repository.

Access, ownership, request status and control-list checks can return before the buffer checks. The enclosing topic already presents the ownership, status and control guards before the buffer guards, and the claims describe those individual checks rather than an error-priority guarantee. The queued invocation and separate completion notification are also supported.

The claim says a state mismatch returns -EACCES without stating that the preceding disconnection check must first pass. When allowDisconnected is false and the camera is disconnected, isAccessAllowed returns -ENODEV before checking state, including when the state also differs. The omission can mislead a caller about the overlapping conditions.
